title: test-capability-inventory
description: Machine shape of the test capability inventory a generated product publishes through its canonical root Gradle alias. The Node runtime validates this schema and the domain-separated inventoryHash only — it never parses Gradle build scripts. Lane task/source-set/compilation names are the frozen pinned-stack decisions proven by the Phase-1 compatibility spike on AGP 9.0.1 + Kotlin 2.3.21 + Gradle 9.1.0: host lane task `testAndroidHostTest` (source set `androidHostTest`, compilation `hostTest`, single enabler `withHostTest`), iOS simulator lane task `iosSimulatorArm64Test`, device lane task `connectedAndroidDeviceTest` via `withDeviceTest` (source set `androidDeviceTest`, compilation `deviceTest` — a standalone instrumented compilation that does NOT include `commonTest`, so shared scenarios reach the device lane only through an explicitly wired dedicated tree; the provider-based `androidDeviceCheck`/`deviceAndroidTest` pair is a proven false-green no-op without configured device providers and must never be an alias target), screenshot wrappers `recordRoborazziAndroidHostTest`/`verifyRoborazziAndroidHostTest` around the same single host task.

generatedBy.description: Exact Gradle task path that produced this inventory.

capabilities.description: Applied opt-in test capabilities. `base` is required whenever any lane is configured; capability conventions never appear without it.

inventoryHash.description: sha256 over `test-capability-inventory\0` + canonical JSON of the inventory without this field. Never comparable with hashes from other domains.

taskPath.description: Exact executable Gradle task path for this lane (e.g. `:feature:testAndroidHostTest`). Aliases depend on the real test task provider; suffix matching is never proof.
